newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST-Swedish Jan c/a seen 6.6 bln skr surplus.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Swedish Jan c/a seen 6.6 bln skr surplus.

text.p: Sweden's January current account is expected to show a surplus of 6.6 billion crowns, according to a Reuter poll of 17 analysts.
Forecasts range between 4.5 billion crowns and eight billion. The January trade surplus amounted to 10.8 billion crowns.
For all of 1997, current account is expected to show a surplus of 53.4 billion crowns, with forecasts ranging from 42.0 billion crowns to 70.0 billion.
In December 1996, the current account showed a surplus of 0.9 billion crowns and in January 1996 the surplus amounted to 7.7 billion. For all of 1996, the surplus was 41.5 billion crowns.
Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, is due to release current account figures on March 19 at 1100 GMT.

Sources: Carnegie, Chase, Consensus, Den Danske Bank, Hagstromer & Qviberg, Handelsbanken, HSBC Midland, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Nomura Bank, PaineWebber, Paribas, Salomon Brothers, S-E-Banken, Sparbanken, Transferator, and Unibank Markets.
Monthly figures only were given by: Consensus, Morgan Stanley, Nomura Bank, PaineWebber, and Paribas
